property_summary: Calling correctRState when R is BELOW_ONE and base reserve is below the base target must set base target to equal base reserve.
After buyShares when totalSupply was zero, _BASE_TARGET_ always equals base balance of the pool.
After buyShares with zero totalSupply, _BASE_TARGET_ must equal baseBalance.
After buyShares when totalSupply was zero, baseTarget must equal baseBalance minus the minted 1001 wei of liquidity to address(0).
After buyShares when totalSupply was zero, _BASE_TARGET_ must equal the base balance of the contract.

After any sequence of public operations, the value of _BASE_TARGET_ must equal _BASE_RESERVE_ whenever _RState_ indicates the ONE state (uint32(1)); the bug by omitting the assignment in the BELOW_ONE->ONE transition breaks this invariant.

After any call to adjustMtFeeRate, _BASE_TARGET_ must equal _BASE_RESERVE_ when RState is ONE and the transition originated from BELOW_ONE; the bug omits this assignment, leaving _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged and causing a mismatch.
